newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BLACKHAWKS END LOSING STREAK AGAINST RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BLACKHAWKS END LOSING STREAK AGAINST RANGERS.

text.p: Jeff Hackett made 36 saves and former Rangers Tony Amonte and Ulf Dahlen scored early in the third period as the Chicago Blackhawks snapped a five-game losing streak by edging New York, 2-1 on Monday.
Hackett, who became the Blackhawks' number one goaltender after they traded Ed Belfour to San Jose early Saturday morning, came up with two stellar stops late in the third period.
"Everyone has to be given the number one opportunity at some point," Blackhawks coach Craig Hartsburg said. "What I'm seeing over the last year and a half ... that's a number one goalie."
In Dallas, Mike Modano had two goals and an assist and Darryl Sydor tied a career high with three assists as the Dallas Stars routed the Los Angeles Kings, 7-2.

Modano's 20th goal of the season, with 28 seconds left in the first period, knotted the score and sparked seven straight Stars' tallies. Dallas had five goals in the second period and extended its unbeaten streak to four games (3-0-1).
Kevin Stevens scored both goals for Los Angeles, which was held to 17 shots.
In Ottawa, Alexei Yashin scored twice and Daniel Alfredsson had a goal and two assists as the Ottawa Senators scored four unanswered goals for a 5-3 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Randy Cunneyworth and Tom Chorske also scored for Ottawa.
Shawn Burr had two goals for the Lightning, who have lost three of four. Tabaracci finished with 26 saves.

"Sometimes teams tend to sit back when you start with two quick goals," said Tampa Bay's John Cullen, who had two assists. "But we're all professionals, we should know that a team like the Senators are going to come back."
In St Louis, Teemu Selanne had two goals and an assist and Guy Hebert stopped 38 shots, leading the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim to a 4-1 victory over the St. Louis Blues.
Dmitri Mironov and Sean Pronger also scored for the Ducks, who improved to 5-2-1 in their last eight games.
Brett Hull scored his team-leading 27th goal for St. Louis, which had its four-game winning streak broken. The Blues lost for just the third time in 12 games (7-3-2).
In Toronto, Craig Billington made 32 saves and Adam Deadmarsh scored 2:17 into the third period to snap a tie as the Colorado Avalanche beat the Toronto Maple Leafs 5-2.

Toronto centre Jamie Baker tried to clear the puck from the left boards, but Deadmarsh streaked down the slot, stole it and snapped a wrist shot over goaltender Felix Potvin's glove for his 20th goal and a 3-2 lead.
"Obviously it was a mistake," Baker said. "Unfortunately, it cost us the game. I'm the goat tonight, I made a mistake and it cost us the game."

In Vancouver, Kirk McLean stopped 32 shots and assisted on Russ Courtnall's go-ahead goal early in the second period as the Vancouver Canucks defeated San Jose 5-2, spoiling Ed Belfour's debut with the Sharks.
McLean turned aside all 19 shots he faced over the final two periods, helping Vancouver improve to 14-2-1 at home against the Sharks.
